h1: LIC Bonus Rates 2026: Latest Slabs, How They're Calculated & What They Mean for Your Maturity
byline: If you own an LIC policy, you've probably seen 'bonus' on your documents — but do you know what rate you're actually getting and how it impacts your final payout? Let me break it all down.

sections.title: First: The Two Types of LIC Bonus (Don't Confuse Them)

content.text: There is currently a lot of confusion online about 'LIC Bonus' — because the term refers to two completely different things.

items.title: 1. The Shareholder Corporate Bonus (Stock Market)
items.text: For equity shareholders of LIC trading on NSE/BSE (NSE: LICI), the Board approved a 1:1 corporate bonus share issue with record date May 29, 2026. Your share count doubled, price adjusted 50% down. This is a stock market liquidity action — it does not affect your insurance policy in any way.

items.title: 2. The Policyholder Actuarial Bonus (This Article)
items.text: This is the annual bonus declared for LIC insurance policyholders. It is a share of the valuation surplus from LIC's life fund, distributed to holders of 'participating' (with-profit) policies like Jeevan Anand, Jeevan Labh, and New Endowment. This is what determines your maturity payout — and this is what we cover here.

sections.title: How LIC Actuarial Bonuses Are Declared

content.text: Every March 31st, LIC's actuarial team values all assets and liabilities of the life fund. By statute, LIC must distribute 95% of the participating fund surplus to policyholders — the remaining 5% goes to the government as promoter.

This surplus is declared every year on September 1st as a Simple Reversionary Bonus (SRB). Once declared, this bonus is legally guaranteed (vested) in your policy and is paid at maturity, death, or surrender.

items: Simple Reversionary Bonus (SRB): Annual bonus declared as ₹X per ₹1,000 of Sum Assured. Does NOT compound.
Interim Bonus: Applied when a policy matures or death occurs between two annual declaration dates.
Final Additional Bonus (FAB): One-time terminal bonus paid only on policies completing 15+ years. Scales exponentially with tenure.
Loyalty Addition (LA): Certain plans pay a one-time addition on exit instead of annual SRB.

sections.title: The Game-Changing Sum Assured Step-Up Slabs

content.text: In recent valuations, LIC introduced a tiered step-up structure to reward higher coverage amounts. This means policyholders with larger Sum Assured (SA) get a higher bonus rate per ₹1,000.

items.title: Standard Two-Slab Structure (Most Plans)
items.text:
Slab A (SA < ₹5,00,000): Base bonus rate.
Slab B (SA ≥ ₹5,00,000): Base rate + ₹1 per ₹1,000 SA step-up.

items.title: Jeevan Labh Three-Slab Structure (Plan 736/936)
items.text:
Slab A (SA < ₹5,00,000): Base rate.
Slab B (₹5L to < ₹10L): Base + ₹1 per ₹1,000 SA.
Slab C (SA ≥ ₹10,00,000): Base + ₹2 per ₹1,000 SA.

For a ₹10 Lakh SA on Jeevan Labh (25-year term), the +₹2 step-up adds ₹2,000 extra per year — or ₹50,000 extra at maturity before terminal bonuses.

sections.title: Final Additional Bonus (FAB) — The Terminal Reward That Can Add Lakhs

content.text: The FAB is a one-time terminal payout added only at maturity or death — but only if your policy has run for 15+ years. It scales exponentially. The longer you stay invested, the bigger the jump.

content.footer: Notice the jump from 20 years (₹70) to 25 years (₹450) for SA ≥ ₹2L — that's a 540% increase in FAB for just 5 extra years. This is why surrendering a long-running policy near maturity is almost always a bad idea.

sections.title: Real Calculation: How to Find Your LIC Maturity Value
sections.description: Let's walk through a complete worked example so you can replicate it for your own policy.

items.title: Scenario: Rohan, Age 30 — LIC New Jeevan Anand (Plan 915)
Step 1 — Calculate Annual Simple Reversionary Bonus
items.text:
Formula: (Sum Assured ÷ 1,000) × Bonus Rate

Since SA = ₹10,00,000 (≥ ₹5L), Rohan qualifies for the step-up slab. Rate for 25-year term = ₹47 per ₹1,000 SA.

Annual SRB = (10,00,000 ÷ 1,000) × 47 = ₹47,000 per year
Total SRB over 25 years = ₹47,000 × 25 = ₹11,75,000

items.title: Step 2 — Calculate Final Additional Bonus (FAB)
items.text:
SA ≥ ₹2 Lakh, completed term = 25 years → FAB rate = ₹450 per ₹1,000 SA

FAB = (10,00,000 ÷ 1,000) × 450 = ₹4,50,000

items.title: Step 3 — Total Maturity Payout
items.text:
Maturity = Sum Assured + Total SRB + FAB

= ₹10,00,000 + ₹11,75,000 + ₹4,50,000 = ₹26,25,000

Rohan paid ~₹46,000/year × 25 years = ₹11,50,000 in premiums. Maturity amount = ₹26.25 Lakhs. Effective IRR ≈ 5.2% to 5.5% per annum.

sections.title: The Compounding Trap: Why 5% IRR Hurts More Than You Think

content.text: Here's the critical problem with LIC's Simple Reversionary Bonus system: it does not compound. Every year, Rohan earns ₹47,000 — but that ₹47,000 just sits in LIC's reserves earning nothing extra. Compare that to an equity mutual fund SIP where your gains themselves earn gains.

content.footer: By year 25, the compounding advantage creates a wealth gap of over ₹1.24 Crore on the same ₹10,000/month commitment. This is the hidden cost of bundling insurance with investment.

sections.title: Tax Rules on LIC Bonus & Maturity: Income Tax Act 2025

rows: Deduction up to ₹1,50,000 on eligible premiums
Maturity proceeds tax-free if annual premium ≤ ₹5 Lakh
Death benefit 100% tax-free regardless of premium size

items.title: The ₹5 Lakh Premium Cap Rule (Post April 2023)
items.text: If you bought a traditional LIC policy on or after April 1, 2023, and your aggregate annual premium across all such policies exceeds ₹5,00,000, the maturity returns are fully taxable at your income slab rate (as 'Income from Other Sources').

items.title: TDS on Taxable LIC Payouts
items.text:
Resident with PAN: 5% TDS on net profit (maturity – total premiums paid) if profit > ₹1 Lakh.
Resident without PAN: Flat 20% TDS on full payout.
NRI: Flat 30% TDS + surcharges + cess.

sections.title: 4 Costly Mistakes LIC Policyholders Make with Bonuses

items: Treating bonus as compound growth: LIC bonuses are simple interest on your flat Sum Assured. The ₹47,000/year Rohan earns never earns interest-on-interest — unlike equity MF returns that compound year after year.
Surrendering in the first 3 years: You lose 30–50% of all premiums paid as surrender charges. If you need to exit, always wait for 3 full years. Better still, convert to 'Paid-Up' status.
Confusing shareholder bonus with policyholder bonus: The May 2026 1:1 bonus share issue benefited LIC equity shareholders — it has zero impact on your insurance policy's maturity value.
Ignoring inflation drag: India's CPI averages 5–5.5% annually. An LIC IRR of 5–5.5% means your real (inflation-adjusted) return is essentially zero over 20+ years.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions: LIC Bonus Rates

items.q: What is the current LIC bonus rate in 2026?
items.a: LIC declares Simple Reversionary Bonus rates annually on September 1st. For 2025–26, rates range from ₹35 to ₹49 per ₹1,000 of Sum Assured depending on the plan, policy term, and Sum Assured slab. For example, LIC New Jeevan Anand (Plan 915) with a 25-year term and SA ≥ ₹5 Lakh earns ₹47 per ₹1,000.

items.q: How do I calculate my LIC policy bonus?
items.a: The formula is: Annual Reversionary Bonus = (Sum Assured ÷ 1,000) × Bonus Rate. For example, if your Sum Assured is ₹10,00,000 and the declared bonus rate is ₹47 per ₹1,000, your annual bonus = (10,00,000 ÷ 1,000) × 47 = ₹47,000.

items.q: Does the LIC shareholder bonus affect my insurance policy?
items.a: No. The 1:1 bonus share issue in May 2026 was a stock market action for LIC equity shareholders (NSE: LICI). It has absolutely no impact on the maturity value, bonus rates, or surrender value of your LIC insurance policy.

items.q: What is the difference between Simple Reversionary Bonus and Final Additional Bonus?
items.a: A Simple Reversionary Bonus (SRB) is declared annually and added to your policy throughout the term. A Final Additional Bonus (FAB) is a one-time terminal payout added only at maturity or death — and only if your policy has run for at least 15 years. FAB rates scale exponentially with tenure.

No. Traditional LIC participating policies use Simple Reversionary Bonuses calculated on your flat, original Sum Assured. There is no compounding — the annual bonus does not earn further returns on itself, unlike equity mutual fund SIPs.

items.q: Is LIC maturity amount taxable in 2026?
items.a: Under the Income Tax Act 2025 (Schedule II), LIC maturity proceeds are tax-free only if your aggregate annual premium on all traditional policies does not exceed ₹5,00,000. If it exceeds this cap, the net profit is taxed at your income slab rate. Death benefits remain 100% tax-free regardless.

items.q: How much TDS is deducted on LIC maturity payouts?
items.a: For resident policyholders with PAN, 5% TDS is deducted from the net profit (maturity amount minus total premiums paid), provided the net profit exceeds ₹1,00,000. Without PAN, flat 20% TDS applies on the full payout.

items.q: Can I withdraw my accrued LIC bonus before maturity?
items.a: No. LIC bonuses are credited to your policy record internally each year and are locked in until the policy terminates — either at maturity, death claim, or early surrender. Partial withdrawals of accrued bonuses are not permitted.

items.q: What is the benefit of a higher Sum Assured for LIC bonus?
items.a: LIC uses a tiered step-up structure. Policyholders with SA ≥ ₹5 Lakh receive +₹1 per ₹1,000 SA over the base rate on most plans. On Jeevan Labh, SA ≥ ₹10 Lakh earns +₹2 per ₹1,000 SA — adding up to ₹50,000 extra at maturity on a 25-year policy.

items.q: Which LIC plan has the highest bonus rate?
items.a: Among actively sold plans, LIC Jeevan Labh (Plan 936) with a 25-year term and SA ≥ ₹10 Lakh earns the highest SRB of ₹49 per ₹1,000 SA. Combined with high FAB rates at 25 years (₹450 per ₹1,000 for SA ≥ ₹2L), it is one of the better-performing traditional plans.

sections.title: The Verdict: How to Optimize Your Portfolio Around LIC Bonuses

content.text: LIC's guaranteed, sovereign-backed bonuses provide peace of mind — but they come at a steep opportunity cost over 20+ years. The optimal strategy isn't to abandon LIC entirely; it's to unbundle your capital.

items.title: Buy Pure Term Insurance for Protection
items.description: A ₹1 Crore term cover at age 30 costs just ₹10,000–₹12,000/year. Maximum protection, minimum cost. This is what LIC excels at.

items.title: Invest the Surplus in Equity Mutual Fund SIPs
items.description: Redirect the premium you were paying for an endowment plan into a diversified equity SIP. Over 25 years at 12% CAGR, this builds ₹1.9 Crore on a ₹10,000/month commitment — vs ₹26 Lakhs from a traditional plan.

items.title: If You Already Hold a Long-Running LIC Policy
items.description: Don't surrender a policy that is 10+ years old — especially if it's within 5 years of maturity. The FAB rate jump between 20 and 25 years is massive. Let it run to maturity and collect the terminal bonus.
